about.title: Pacifica Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Pacifica residents rely on nearby San Mateo County medical facilities for everything from routine care to emergency treatment after a crash on Highway 1 or Sharp Park Road. Most of the time, that care meets the standard patients expect. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgical step is skipped, or medication is mismanaged, the consequences can follow a patient long after they've left the exam room. California law recognizes that a bad medical outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — there has to be a deviation from the accepted standard of care, and that usually takes a qualified medical expert to establish. If you're a Pacifica resident trying to understand whether what happened to you crosses that line, we can review your situation at no charge and explain what your options might be under California's malpractice framework.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Starts Sooner Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Waiting to sort things out on your own can cost you the ability to pursue a claim at all.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed in California, the law requires 90 days' advance notice to the provider. Getting that notice right, and timed correctly, is part of why early legal guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California malpractice cases nearly always need a qualified medical expert to show the care fell below an accepted standard. We can help arrange that kind of review before deciding how to move forward.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in Pacifica — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor result alone isn't enough; there has to be evidence the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. That's why a medical expert typically needs to review the records before anyone can say whether a claim exists.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened, whichever comes first. There are some exceptions, so it's worth getting this reviewed by an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Are there limits on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: Yes — California caps non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.
